strategy.summary: Reproduce sympy/sympy#28307 hang/blocking in Expr.__int__ when converting a log-based integer expression to int for large n (e.g., 857). Build and run SymPy’s core test suite on the buggy revision so the added test fails (hang), and on the fixed revision so it passes (returns and asserts).

pip_packages: sympy==1.14.0 (install for baseline availability only; main reproduction should use the git checkout and pip install .)
system_packages: gfortran (optional; SymPy may compile some components)
build_commands: # optional: build docs (not required for tests)
pinned_because: Python 3.12.10 is mentioned in the issue context as the observed environment for the hang on Apple Silicon; the reproduction should be attempted with this exact Python if possible.
The test is inside sympy/core/tests/test_expr.py and exercises Expr.__int__; therefore SymPy must be installed from source at the buggy commit and later at the fixed commit.
The specific hang trigger is associated with evaluating the log-based expression for large n; test execution must run the added assertion in test_round().

strategy.reproducing_test: The project’s own regression test to add to sympy/core/tests/test_expr.py inside test_round(): compute a(n) via the given formula using sympy log/Rational/sqrt and assert a(857) equals the provided large integer literal.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (git checkout 7bf4a6bf3544), running the test command hangs/blocks when executing the new assert a(857)==a857 (i.e., the test does not complete). On the fixed revision (the commit corresponding to PR sympy/sympy#28307), the same test completes and the assertion passes (a(857) equals the provided integer literal).
strategy.numerical_probe: Not used as a separate check. The only graded transition is whether the test completes and the single equality assertion succeeds; on the buggy revision it fails by hanging/locking during int-conversion of the expression for n=857.
risks: The evidence does not specify the exact fixed commit hash for PR sympy/sympy#28307; you must identify the merged commit (or the PR head commit) that contains the fix, otherwise the 'passes_on_fixed' transition cannot be validated.

The hang/blocking is described as occurring under Python 3.12.10 on Apple Silicon (M2 Pro). If the issue is platform/toolchain dependent (e.g., different gmpy/mpmath build, CPU arch), the buggy behavior might not reproduce identically on other hardware or Python versions.
If your local SymPy checkout already contains additional patches compared to the buggy commit, ensure you have a clean git checkout at exactly 7bf4a6bf3544 before running the test.
Doc build steps are irrelevant to this bug; avoid changing test environment/threads (no parallel pytest) to reduce nondeterminism.
The test must execute the new code path in test_round; using -k filters that skip test_round would not reproduce the defect. Keep the provided test_command.

oracle.reference_source: The regression test includes an exact integer literal expected value for a(857). The oracle is exact equality of the computed a(857) and the provided literal.
oracle.why: The test directly asserts integer equality; no tolerance/rounding check is used.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion `assert a(857) == a857` does not complete because converting the constructed expression to int via Expr.__int__ hangs/locks for n=857 on the buggy revision, so the test process stalls and never reaches the assertion evaluation.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After applying the fix from sympy/sympy#28307 (fixed revision), converting the same expression to int completes promptly and `a(857)` equals the provided large integer literal, so the test completes successfully.
